title: After large western U.S. wildfires, baseflow and quickflow rose by similar fractions and the baseflow index did not change (50 CAMELS fire events, 1985-2022, daily USGS flow)
abstract: An earlier SCI study (sci:07ca7c27) found +21 % (1985-2019 fires) and +37 % (2020-2022 fires) annual runoff in post-fire years 1-6 in western U.S. CAMELS reference basins with 20 % or more burned. We tested which part of the daily hydrograph carries this increase. We downloaded USGS NWIS daily discharge for 330 western CAMELS gauges (water years 1951-2025), separated baseflow and quickflow with the Lyne-Hollick filter, and kept the events, climate model, regional adjustment and pseudo-event null of the earlier study unchanged. We wrote the predictions before the analysis. The new data reproduce the earlier totals (+0.187 and +0.318 log units, same 33 and 17 events). For all 50 events, baseflow increased by +0.252 log units and quickflow by +0.233 (null 95 % ranges about +-0.08). The baseflow index did not change (+0.007, fire-cluster bootstrap 95 % CI -0.007 to +0.020; 10 % burn threshold with 94 events: +0.003, CI -0.008 to +0.015). Thus the infiltration-loss prediction of a lower baseflow index failed. Baseflow carried 0.57 (CI 0.46-0.80) of the +52.7 mm per year excess; the pre-fire baseflow share was 0.46. The 7-day low flow had the largest relative gain (+64 %), the annual maximum daily flow the smallest (+17 %, CI +0.7 to +36 %). Flow timing did not change (-0.5 days, CI -5.9 to +4.7). The extra baseflow depth did not depend on post-fire precipitation (+0.3 +- 12.9 mm per unit ln P), so its relative size was larger in dry years; this explains the dry-year pattern that the earlier study did not resolve. These results agree best with reduced evapotranspiration. For the 17 events of 2020-2022, quickflow increased more than baseflow (log difference -0.087, CI -0.154 to -0.022) and timing was 8 days later; this post hoc difference was not clear with the 10 % threshold. Limitations: the filter is a signal separation, not a groundwater measurement; daily means cannot show sub-daily flood peaks; 42 fire clusters; perimeter burn area without severity; no test of gauge rating changes. Code, the derived component table, aggregate results and figures are included; raw NWIS files are external with hashes.

citations.reason: We reuse its burned-fraction, climate and fire-cluster tables and its event and null method, reproduce its runoff excess with new daily data, and decompose the excess into hydrograph parts. We explain its unresolved dry-year pattern.
Source of the basin climate table (nClimGrid) and of the NWIS retrieval method; our total runoff agrees with its runoff table.
Sub-daily post-fire debris-flow thresholds; our daily-scale result does not test such short events.
